'''Kiros T. Berhane''' is an [[Ethiopians|Ethiopian]]–American [[Biostatistics|biostatistician]] noted for methodological work in [[environmental epidemiology]] and for team-science contributions linking ambient and traffic-related air pollution to impaired lung-function growth in adolescents—and later demonstrating lung growth improvements with cleaner air.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gauderman |first=W. J. |date=2015 |title=Association of improved air quality with lung development in children |journal=The New England Journal of Medicine |volume=372 |issue=10 |pages=905–913 |doi=10.1056/NEJMoa1414123 |pmid=25738666}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gauderman |first=W. J. |date=2007 |title=Effect of exposure to traffic on lung development from 10 to 18 years of age |journal=The Lancet |volume=369 |issue=9561 |pages=571–577 |doi=10.1016/S0140-6736(07)60037-3 |pmid=17307103}}</ref> As of 2025 he is Chair of Biostatistics at [[Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health|Columbia University's Mailman School of Public Health]] and serves on the ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' magazine Board of Reviewing Editors; he is also an elected Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] and of the [[American Statistical Association]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025 |title=Editors and Advisory Boards — Masthead (PDF) |url=https://www.science.org/cms/asset/3d727b30-9faa-48f3-babe-307f3e21e95b/masthead.pdf |access-date=2025-11-26 |website=Science |publisher=AAAS}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-27 |title=Eight Columbians Named AAAS Fellows |url=https://news.columbia.edu/news/eight-columbians-named-aaas-fellows |access-date=2025-11-26 |website=Columbia News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-07-10 |title=Biostatistics Professor Honored for Scientific Contributions |url=https://hscnews.usc.edu/biostatistics-professor-honored-for-scientific-contributions |access-date=2025-11-26 |website=Keck/USC Health Sciences News}}</ref>

== Education ==
Berhane earned a [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] in statistics and mathematics from [[Addis Ababa University]], an MS in statistics from the [[University of Guelph]], and a PhD in biostatistics from the [[University of Toronto]]. He completed a postdoctoral fellowship at [[Johns Hopkins University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kiros Berhane, PhD |url=https://www.publichealth.columbia.edu/profile/kiros-berhane-phd |access-date=November 26, 2025 |website=Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health}}</ref><ref name="UBPerry">{{cite web |title=2024: Kiros Berhane, PhD |url=https://publichealth.buffalo.edu/home/news-events/annual-events/perry-lecture/perry-lecturers/2024.html |access-date=2025-11-26 |website=School of Public Health and Health Professions |publisher=University at Buffalo}}</ref><ref name="NASBio">{{cite web |title=Kiros T. Berhane |url=https://www.nationalacademies.org/projects/DELS-BEST-20-06 |access-date=2025-11-26 |website=Advancing the Framework for Assessing Causality of Health and Welfare Effects to Inform National Ambient Air Quality Standard Reviews |publisher=National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine}}</ref>

== Career ==
Berhane joined the Graduate School of Public Health at the [[University of Pittsburgh]], where he was an assistant professor of family medicine and [[clinical epidemiology]] in the School of Medicine and an assistant professor of biostatistics, with research interests in [[nonparametric regression]], [[longitudinal data]] analysis, and time-series methods.<ref name="PittBulletin">{{cite web |title=Departments and Programs: Department of Biostatistics |url=https://www.bulletins.pitt.edu/archive/health/hh1.html |access-date=2025-11-26 |website=Graduate School of Public Health Bulletin |publisher=University of Pittsburgh}}</ref>

He later moved to the [[USC Keck School of Medicine|Keck School of Medicine]] of the [[University of Southern California]], where he became a professor of [[Preventive healthcare|preventive medicine]] in the Division of Biostatistics and directed the school's epidemiology and biostatistics graduate degree programs.<ref name="USC2017">{{cite news |last=Puro |first=Larissa |date=June 19, 2017 |title=Biostatistics professor honored for scientific contributions |url=https://keck.usc.edu/news/biostatistics-professor-honored-for-scientific-contributions/ |access-date=2025-11-26 |work=Keck School of Medicine Newsroom |publisher=University of Southern California}}</ref><ref name="NCCOR">{{cite web |title=Investigators |url=https://www.nccor.org/envision/investigators.html |access-date=2025-11-26 |website=NCCOR Envision |publisher=National Collaborative on Childhood Obesity Research}}</ref> From 2011 to 2019 he served as director of graduate programs in biostatistics and epidemiology at USC.<ref name="DSIAfrica">{{cite web |title=Prof Kiros Berhane Biography |url=https://dsi-africa.org/dsi-2nd-consortium/biography/77 |access-date=2025-11-26 |website=DS-I Africa}}</ref> At USC he served as lead biostatistician for the Children's Health Study (CHS), a series of longitudinal cohort studies that provided evidence that long-term exposure to ambient air pollution slows lung function growth and worsens respiratory symptoms in children.<ref>{{cite web |date=February 10, 2020 |title=Biostatistics Chair Embraces Complexity |url=https://www.publichealth.columbia.edu/news/biostatistics-chair-embraces-complexity |access-date=November 26, 2025 |website=Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Gauderman |first=W. James |author2=Gilliland, G. Frank |author3=Vora, Hita |author4=Avol, Edward |author5=Stram, Daniel |author6=McConnell, Rob |author7=Thomas, Duncan |author8=Lurmann, Fred |author9=Margolis, Helene G. |author10=Rappaport, Edward B. |author11=Berhane, Kiros |author12=Peters, John M. |year=2002 |title=Association between air pollution and lung function growth in southern California children: results from a second cohort |journal=American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine |volume=166 |issue=1 |pages=76–84 |doi=10.1164/rccm.2111021 |pmid=12091175}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=The Children's Health Study {{!}} California Air Resources Board |url=https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/resources/documents/childrens-health-study |access-date=2025-11-27 |website=ww2.arb.ca.gov}}</ref>

In January 2020 Berhane was appointed Cynthia and Robert Citrone-Roslyn and Leslie Goldstein Professor of Biostatistics and Chair of the Department of Biostatistics at the Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health.<ref>{{cite web |title=Committee Member Biographies |url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK588331/ |access-date=November 26, 2025 |website=National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Faculty and Staff – Center for Achieving Resilience in Climate and Health |url=https://www.publichealth.columbia.edu/research/centers/center-climate-health/people/faculty |access-date=November 26, 2025 |website=Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health}}</ref> He directs the Center for Achieving Resilience in Climate and Health (C-ARCH) at Columbia, a climate and health "solutions lab" he co-leads with environmental health scientist [[Darby Jack]] that develops and evaluates strategies to build resilience to climate-related health risks, with an emphasis on partnerships with governments and communities and on research capacity building in regions such as [[East Africa|Eastern Africa]].<ref>{{cite web |date=February 26, 2025 |title=Columbia Mailman Launches Climate & Health Center |url=https://www.publichealth.columbia.edu/news/columbia-mailman-launches-climate-health-center |access-date=November 26, 2025 |website=Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Research – Center for Achieving Resilience in Climate and Health |url=https://www.publichealth.columbia.edu/research/centers/c-arch/research |access-date=November 26, 2025 |website=Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health}}</ref><ref name="UBPerry" /><ref name="NASBio" />

Berhane serves on various leadership capacities within the [[National Institutes of Health|NIH]]-funded [[Harnessing Data Science for Health Discovery and Innovation in Africa|Data Science Initiative for Africa]] (DS-I Africa), such as the Contact [[Principal investigator|Principal Investigator]] of the ''Advancing Public Health Research for Eastern Africa through Data Science Training'' (APHREA-DST) training project, and as a member of the steering committee for the DS-I Africa Consortium.<ref>{{Cite web |title=APHREA-DST {{!}} DS-I Africa |url=https://dsi-africa.org/project/19 |access-date=2025-11-29 |website=dsi-africa.org}}</ref>

Outside academia, Berhane writes poetry in [[Tigrinya language|Tigrinya]], [[Amharic]] and English and shares his work on the Ethiopian online literary site ''Meskot'' and on his [[YouTube]] "Literature Channel".<ref>{{cite web |title=Meskot Poetry Page |url=https://www.meskot.com/poetry_page.htm |access-date=2025-11-27 |website=Meskot}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Kiros Berhane – Literature Channel |url=https://www.youtube.com/%40mezgeb123/videos |access-date=2025-11-27 |website=YouTube}}</ref>

== Research and contributions ==

=== Children's Health Study findings on air pollution and lung growth ===
As a biostatistician in the CHS, he co-authored studies that provided longitudinal evidence that contemporary ambient air pollution slows adolescents' lung development (''[[The New England Journal of Medicine|NEJM]]'', 2004), and that living near heavy traffic is associated with impaired lung-function growth (''[[The Lancet]]'', 2007).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gauderman |first=W. J. |last2=Avol |first2=E. |last3=Gilliland |first3=F. |last4=Vora |first4=H. |last5=Thomas |first5=D. |last6=Berhane |first6=K. |date=September 9, 2004 |title=The effect of air pollution on lung development from 10 to 18 years of age |url=https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa040610 |journal=The New England Journal of Medicine |volume=351 |issue=11 |pages=1057–1067 |doi=10.1056/NEJMoa040610 |pmid=15356303}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gauderman |first=W. J. |last2=Vora |first2=H. |last3=McConnell |first3=R. |last4=Berhane |first4=K. |last5=Gilliland |first5=F. |last6=Thomas |first6=D. C. |last7=Lurmann |first7=F. |last8=Avol |first8=E. |date=February 17, 2007 |title=Effect of exposure to traffic on lung development from 10 to 18 years of age: a cohort study |url=https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140673607600373/abstract |journal=The Lancet |volume=369 |issue=9561 |pages=571–577 |doi=10.1016/S0140-6736(07)60037-3 |pmid=17307103}}</ref> He also co-authored the ''NEJM'' report showing that cleaner regional air was associated with measurably better lung growth in adolescents (2015); contemporaneous coverage described it as "for the first time" linking improved air quality to better lung development in children.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gauderman |first=W. J. |last2=Urman |first2=R. |last3=Avol |first3=E. |last4=Berhane |first4=K. |last5=McConnell |first5=R. |last6=Rappaport |first6=E. |last7=Tzezoumis |first7=K. |last8=Chung |first8=J. H. |last9=Gilliland |first9=F. D. |date=March 5, 2015 |title=Association of Improved Air Quality with Lung Development in Children |url=https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1414123 |journal=The New England Journal of Medicine |volume=372 |issue=10 |pages=905–913 |doi=10.1056/NEJMoa1414123 |pmid=25738666}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Barboza |first=Tony |date=March 4, 2015 |title=Cleaner air is linked to stronger lungs in Southern California children |url=https://www.latimes.com/local/lanow/la-me-clean-air-lungs-children-20150304-story.html |access-date=November 26, 2025 |work=Los Angeles Times}}</ref>

=== Methodological contributions ===
Berhane has developed and helped spread new statistical methods for studying how health measures change over time and how the timing and amount of exposure to workplace and environmental hazards are linked to later disease risk. With [[Nuoo-Ting Molitor]], he introduced an approach that looks at the overall shape of a person's [[Growth curve (biology)|growth curve]] over time (for example, when growth speeds up most) and connects those features to environmental conditions such as air pollution; this work grew out of analyses of lung growth in the CHS.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Berhane |first=K. |last2=Molitor |first2=N.-T. |date=2008 |title=A Bayesian approach to functional-based multilevel modeling of longitudinal data: Applications to environmental epidemiology |journal=Biostatistics |volume=9 |issue=4 |pages=686–699 |doi=10.1093/biostatistics/kxm059 |pmc=2733176 |pmid=18349036}}</ref>

In studies where cancers may appear many years after exposure, he co-authored one of the early methods that uses [[Curve|smooth curves]] ("splines") to describe how cancer risk changes with time since exposure, using data from the Colorado Plateau Uranium Miners cohort.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hauptmann |first=Michael |last2=Berhane |first2=Kiros |last3=Langholz |first3=Bryan |last4=Lubin |first4=Jay H. |date=2001 |title=Using splines to analyse latency in the Colorado Plateau Uranium Miners cohort |journal=Journal of Epidemiology and Biostatistics |volume=6 |issue=6 |pages=417–424 |doi=10.1080/135952201317225444 |pmid=11859827}}</ref> He later helped develop a more flexible version of this idea that looks at age, time since exposure, and exposure level together, to better describe how long-term or repeated exposures affect disease risk (''[[Statistics in Medicine (journal)|Statistics in Medicine]]'', 2008).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Berhane |first=Kiros |last2=Hauptmann |first2=Michael |last3=Langholz |first3=Bryan |date=November 20, 2008 |title=Using tensor product splines in modeling exposure–time–response relationships: Application to the Colorado Plateau Uranium Miners cohort |journal=Statistics in Medicine |volume=27 |issue=26 |pages=5484–5496 |doi=10.1002/sim.3354 |pmc=3032879 |pmid=18613262}}</ref>

He has written about statistical challenges in long-term studies of air pollution and children's health, including how to capture adolescent growth spurts and other biologically meaningful features of children's lung function over time.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Berhane |first=Kiros |last2=Gauderman |first2=W. James |last3=Stram |first3=Daniel O. |last4=Thomas |first4=Duncan C. |date=2004 |title=Statistical Issues in Studies of the Long-Term Effects of Air Pollution: The Southern California Children's Health Study |journal=Statistical Science |volume=19 |issue=3 |pages=414–449 |jstor=4144392 }}</ref>

Berhane has also contributed to genetic and gene–environment interaction studies in [[asthma]] and [[childhood obesity]], including work on [[nitric oxide synthase]] and [[arginase]] [[Polymorphism (biology)|polymorphisms]] and exhaled nitric oxide in children, and on [[TGF beta 1|TGF-β1]] promoter variants and susceptibility to early-onset childhood asthma.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Salam |first1=M. T. |last2=Gauderman |first2=W. J. |last3=McConnell |first3=R. |last4=Gruisin |first4=H. |last5=Berhane |first5=K. |last6=Gilliland |first6=F. D. |year=2011 |title=Genetic variants in nitric oxide synthase and arginase genes and childhood asthma and exhaled nitric oxide levels |journal=Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology |volume=127 |issue=2 |pages=369–376.e5 |doi=10.1016/j.jaci.2010.10.016 |pmid=21167574}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Li |first1=Ying |last2=Wang |first2=S. |last3=Zhang |first3=Y. |last4=Berhane |first4=K. |last5=Gilliland |first5=F. D. |year=2012 |title=Association of TGF-β1 C-509T polymorphism and childhood asthma: modification by environmental tobacco smoke |journal=Pharmacogenetics and Genomics |volume=22 |issue=2 |pages=114–121 |doi=10.1097/FPC.0b013e32834e1b6b |pmid=22157175}}</ref>

=== Tigray ===
During the 2020–2022 war in the [[Tigray Region|Tigray]] region of Ethiopia, Berhane joined other members of the [[Global Society of Tigray Scholars and Professionals]] in documenting the public health consequences of the conflict, serving as a co-author of a [[The BMJ|BMJ]] ''Global Health'' assessment of war-related damage to Tigray's health system and a subsequent community-based BMJ ''Global Health'' study of war-related sexual and [[Gender-based price discrimination in the United States|gender-based]] violence. He was a signatory to an [[International Diabetes Federation]] appeal calling for urgent restoration of access to [[insulin]] and other essential medicines.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Gesesew |first1=Hailay A. |last2=Berhane |first2=Kiros |last3=Siraj |first3=Elias S. |last4=Siraj |first4=Dawd |last5=Gebregziabher |first5=Mulugeta |last6=Gebre |first6=Yemane G. |last7=Gebreslassie |first7=Samuel A. |last8=Amdes |first8=Fasika |last9=Tesema |first9=Azeb G. |last10=Tesfay |first10=Fisaha H. |date=2021 |title=The impact of war on the health system of the Tigray region in Ethiopia: an assessment |journal=BMJ Global Health |volume=6 |issue=11 |article-number=e007328 |doi=10.1136/bmjgh-2021-007328 |pmc=8611430 |pmid=34815244}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Fisseha |first1=Girmatsion |last2=Gebrehiwot |first2=Teklehaimanot G. |last3=Gebremichael |first3=Gebrekiros G. |last4=Embaye |first4=Kebede E. |last5=Gebreslassie |first5=Aregawi |last6=Abebe |first6=Haftom T. |last7=Haile |first7=Yibrah A. |last8=Gezahegn |first8=Selome |last9=Aregawi |first9=Maru |last10=Berhane |first10=Kiros T. |last11=Godefay |first11=Hagos |last12=Mulugeta |first12=Afework |date=2023 |title=War-related sexual and gender-based violence in Tigray, Northern Ethiopia: a community-based study |journal=BMJ Global Health |volume=8 |issue=7 |article-number=e010270 |doi=10.1136/bmjgh-2022-010270 |pmc=10358141 |pmid=37479499}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=14 January 2022 |title=Call for urgent action to avert avoidable diabetes deaths in Tigray, Ethiopia |url=https://idf.org/news/call-for-urgent-action-to-avert-avoidable-diabetes-deaths-in-tigray-ethiopia/ |access-date=27 November 2025 |website=International Diabetes Federation}}</ref>

== Publications ==

=== Editorial boards ===
Berhane serves on the editorial or advisory boards of several scientific journals. He is an associate editor of the ''[[International Journal of Public Health]]'', and has been a member of the editorial boards of ''Environmental Epidemiology'' and the ''[[Archives of Environmental & Occupational Health]]'', as well as an advisory board member for the ''[[East African Journal of Health Sciences]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=International Journal of Public Health – Editors |url=https://www.ssph-journal.org/journals/international-journal-of-public-health/editors |access-date=2025-11-27 |website=International Journal of Public Health |publisher=Swiss School of Public Health}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Journals Year in Review: 2022 – Environmental Epidemiology |url=https://iseepi.org/journals_year_in_review_2022.php |access-date=2025-11-27 |website=International Society for Environmental Epidemiology}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Archives of Environmental & Occupational Health – Editorial Board |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/vaeh20/about-this-journal |access-date=2025-11-27 |website=Taylor & Francis Online}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Editorial Team |url=https://journal.mu.edu.et/index.php/eajhs/about/editorialTeam |access-date=2025-11-27 |website=East African Journal of Health Sciences}}</ref> He also serves on the Board of Reviewing Editors for ''Science'', published by the American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS).<ref>{{cite web |title=Kiros Berhane, PhD |url=https://www.publichealth.columbia.edu/profile/kiros-berhane-phd |access-date=2025-11-27 |website=Columbia Mailman School of Public Health}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Kiros Berhane |url=https://globalcenters.columbia.edu/content/kiros-berhane |access-date=2025-11-27 |website=Columbia Global Centers}}</ref>

=== Peer-reviewed articles ===
In 2025, [[Google Scholar]] reported an [[h-index]] of 75, [[Author-level metrics|i10-index]] of 174 and 25,366 citations.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kiros Berhane|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=hB2mumYAAAAJ&hl=en|website=scholar.google.com|access-date=2025-11-29}}</ref>

''Selected articles:''
